newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's reviews Sampoerna Baa3 rating.
newsitem.headline: Moody's reviews Sampoerna Baa3 rating.

text.p: Moody's said it had placed on review its Baa3 rating on the long-term debt of Sampoerna International Finance Co B.V.'s US$200 million notes for a possible downgrade.
The rating agency said the notes are unconditionally guaranteed by Indonesian cigarette company P.T. Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna.

It said the review was prompted by a series of announcements by Sampoerna on October 5 that it was convening an extraordinary general meeting. The meeting would address, among other subjects, Moody's said, the "financing and purchase of Astra shares". It added that Sampoerna International had secured a short-term bank facility of US$400 million "designated for the company's corporate development purposes".
Moody's said it changed its rating outlook on Sampoerna's long-term debt from stable to negative in response to the an earlier statement by the company.

In it, Sampoerna said its wholly-owned subsidiary, Sampoerna Investment Corp (BVI), and Sampoerna's president director, Putera Sampoerna, on a private basis, had acquired 2.85 percent and 9.8 percent, respectively, of car assembler P.T. Astra International.

Moody's said these announcements "clearly indicate that Sampoerna intends to pursue a much more aggressive diversification strategy away from its original plan as well as its willingness to use a higher level of debt capacity for this purpose".

Moody's said the review would focus on the prospects for further investment by Sampoerna in Astra and, if the investment materialised, the method of financing, its impact on the predictability of the company's overall cash flow, and the magnitude of additional business and political risk incurred.
